source.citation: Ross PJ (2011), Numerical Solution of the Continuity Equation for Soil Water Flow Using Precomputed Steady-State Fluxes, Vadose Zone Journal 10:760-766

source_structure.cell_balance: finite-volume continuity balance over cell i using q_(i-1/2) and q_(i+1/2)
source_structure.time_point: flux is evaluated at a selected fraction sigma of the time step
source_structure.state_variable: v=theta in unsaturated cells and v=h in saturated cells
source_structure.flux_linearization: q^sigma is approximated from the start-step face flux plus first derivatives with respect to the two endpoint states times sigma times their increments
source_structure.resulting_system: the unknown increments Delta v form a tridiagonal linear system
source_structure.retry_semantics: if state changes are unacceptable, a smaller dt can be solved without recomputing the start-step fluxes or derivatives
source_structure.mass_statement: the discretized continuity equation gives exact mass balance to computational error

not_yet_reconstructed_or_qualified: mixed theta/head matrix coefficients when a cell changes saturation status

interpretation: The executed Gate A harness tests the same algebraic continuity/linearization structure described by Ross 2011, but deliberately replaces the nonlinear precomputed face table with an analytic linear face law. The green Gate A result is therefore valid evidence for conservation and bounded tridiagonal algebra, not evidence for Ross hydraulic fidelity.
